metadata.case_name: Costa Rica vs. Nicaragua / Honduras / Guatemala (Central American exceptionalism)
metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: High-vs-low-middle P1 ordinal prediction. Costa Rica's far higher pre-event P1 (0.605) vs its neighbors (Nicaragua 0.388, Guatemala 0.375, Honduras 0.335) -> gap to the nearest neighbor = 0.217, well beyond the WGI margin (Mod4 does NOT trigger) -> a confident ranking is warranted: Costa Rica should show dramatically better stability and human development.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record (country_ref + years; no embedded indicators). Resolved scores are real MI v2 re-scores. Post-1948 military abolition (Costa Rica) -> 2024; scored ~1996 vs 2024. Costa Rica is the regional exception (Tier 2); the three neighbors are Tier 3 throughout.

pre_event.event_description: Four Central American states a decade after the region's civil wars wound down. Costa Rica (no army since 1948) had consolidated as a stable democracy with region-leading institutions; Nicaragua, Honduras and Guatemala carried weak institutions, high violence and shallow democratic roots.

Costa Rica.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Army abolished 1948 (Art. 12, 1949 Constitution); region-leading control of corruption and rule of law; high human-development trajectory.

Nicaragua.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Fragile post-civil-war democracy; later authoritarian reversion under Ortega.

Honduras.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Weak institutions, very high homicide, 2009 coup.

Guatemala.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. 1996 peace accords ended civil war; weak institutions, high violence, deep human-capital deficit.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Costa Rica > {Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala}; Costa Rica stays Tier 2, the three neighbors stay Tier 3
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: P1 ordinality with a wide, defensible gap (Costa Rica 0.605 vs nearest neighbor 0.388 = 0.217, well beyond the WGI margin -> Mod4 does NOT trigger)
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Any neighbor matches/exceeds Costa Rica's trajectory, or Costa Rica drops to the neighbors' tier

b_violence.prediction: Costa Rica low internal-violence RISK; the low-P1 neighbors carry elevated violence/repression risk
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Costa Rica experiences sustained internal violence, or the neighbors remain as peaceful/stable as Costa Rica

c_convergence.prediction: Divergence: Costa Rica stays well above the neighbor cluster; the MI gap does not close
c_convergence.basis: Wide pre-event P1/MI gap (Costa Rica MI 0.694 vs neighbor cluster 0.475-0.527)
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Convergence: the neighbors close the MI gap to Costa Rica

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Costa Rica: no primary failure dimension (residual exposure = process/electoral, P2). Neighbors fail on P1/institutions (and Nicaragua specifically on accountability/voice -> reversal)
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Costa Rica's stability fails on an institutional pillar, or the neighbors' problems prove non-institutional

e_fragment_count.prediction: N/A (no territorial fragmentation in any of the four)

f_reversal_risk.prediction: Costa Rica low reversal risk; Nicaragua high reversal risk (fragile post-civil-war democracy, accountability deficit)
f_reversal_risk.falsification_condition: Costa Rica backslides, or Nicaragua consolidates as a durable democracy

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: Latent for the low-P1 neighbors (esp. Nicaragua); N/A for Costa Rica
g_suppression_mechanism.falsification_condition: No suppression dynamics emerge in any neighbor

h_substate_turbulence.falsification_condition: Sub-state turbulence emerges in any entity

Costa Rica.outcome_summary: Remained the regional exception (Tier 2): MI 0.694 -> 0.686, P1 0.605 -> 0.616. Continued peaceful turnovers, no army, highest HDI and lowest violence in the region. Stability and human development decisively above all three neighbors throughout.

Nicaragua.outcome_summary: Stayed Tier 3 and reverted to authoritarianism: MI 0.475 -> 0.467, P1 0.388 -> 0.283 (sharp institutional/accountability decline). 2018 crackdown on protests (hundreds killed), Ortega-Murillo consolidation, opposition jailed/exiled, 2021 sham election.

Honduras.outcome_summary: Stayed Tier 3: MI 0.520 -> 0.465, P1 0.335 -> 0.357. 2009 coup, among the world's highest homicide rates, chronic weak institutions and corruption; no state breakup but persistent instability and out-migration.

Guatemala.outcome_summary: Stayed Tier 3: MI 0.527 -> 0.498, P1 0.375 -> 0.373. Persistent weak institutions, corruption (CICIG expelled 2019), high violence and deep human-capital deficit; 2023-24 saw a contested but ultimately respected democratic transition (Arevalo).

a_trajectory.evidence: Costa Rica stayed Tier 2 (MI 0.686) and decisively above all neighbors; Nicaragua/Honduras/Guatemala stayed Tier 3 (post-MI 0.467/0.465/0.498). Full ordering matches the pre-P1 ranking; gap to nearest neighbor never closed.
a_trajectory.explanation: AUTO: top correct (Costa Rica) but sub-ordering differs (pred ['Costa Rica', 'Nicaragua', 'Guatemala', 'Honduras'] vs outcome ['Costa Rica', 'Guatemala', 'Nicaragua', 'Honduras']); often a within-margin sub-pair. | prior: AUTO: top correct (Costa Rica) but sub-ordering differs (pred ['Costa Rica', 'Nicaragua', 'Guatemala', 'Honduras'] vs outcome ['Costa Rica', 'Guatemala', 'Nicaragua', 'Honduras']); often a within-margin sub-pair. | prior: Wide P1 gap mapped to divergent outcomes exactly as pred

analysis.overall_assessment: Textbook regional-exceptionalism confirmation: Costa Rica's far higher P1 mapped to decisively better stability and human development, and the wide gap (Mod4 correctly silent) justified a confident ranking that held across all three neighbors. Nicaragua's authoritarian reversion also vindicated the reversal-risk call.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: A four-way ordinal test where a single high-P1 state and three low-middle-P1 neighbors share region, era, and post-conflict history: institutional quality, not geography or shared shock, sets the outcome. It also pairs a wide-gap confident ranking (the Mod4 NON-abstention complement to case36's abstention) with a correct within-set reversal-risk call (Nicaragua).
analysis.baseline_impact: None; reinforces P1 ordinality at a wide gap and the Safeguard C reversal-risk logic.
